metadata = {"protocolName": "PCR_setup_96", "apiLevel": "2.19"}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tips = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_300ul", 1)
    source_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 2)
    reservoir = protocol.load_labware("nest_12_reservoir_15ml", 3)
    pcr_plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt", 4)
    
    # Define master mix
    master_mix = protocol.define_liquid(
        name="master mix", description="PCR master mix", display_color="#FF0000"
    )
    reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix, volume=2000)
    
    # Define sample liquids (one per well) and load them
    for well in source_plate.wells():
        sample_liquid = protocol.define_liquid(
            name=f"sample_{well.name}", description=f"Sample from {well.name}", display_color="#000000"
        )
        well.load_liquid(liquid=sample_liquid, volume=100)
    
    # Load pipette
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tips])
    p300.pick_up_tip()
    
    # Transfer 18 ul master mix + 2 ul template to each well
    for well in pcr_plate.wells():
        # Add 18 ul master mix
        p300.aspirate(18, reservoir["A1"])
        p300.dispense(18, well)
        # Add 2 ul template from matching source well
        p300.aspirate(2, source_plate[well.name])
        p300.dispense(2, well)
    
    p300.drop_tip()"}

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 96 stocks
   line 36:  p20.aspirate(2, source_plate[well_name])
   At line 36 the tip went into sample_A1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample_A2 (well A2 in slot
   2), sample_A3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample_A4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 92 more while it
   still carried master mix (well A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step (this line did it 96
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does
   not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no
   longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 36 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [783bf5e8376a]

2. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 96 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 34:  p20.dispense(18, pcr_plate[well_name])
   At line 34 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 4), and 96 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 88 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 18 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [f67c87407bbb]

3. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 96 wells never mixed after sample_A1, sample_A2, sample_A3,
sample_A4 and 92 more went in (10% of the well)
   line 37:  p20.dispense(2, pcr_plate[well_name])
   At line 37 the robot added sample_A1, sample_A2, sample_A3, sample_A4 and 92 more to
   wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4, which already held master mix
   (this line did it 96 times). The addition was 10% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in slot 4 after line 37:
   `mix_after=(5, 16)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 16, well)`, with the volume about
   80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [888c6ba5e090]

can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
